# zuid

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuid/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuid/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedrobtz/zuid/gh-pages/badges/coverage.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuid/actions/workflows/coverage.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

Identifiers arrive as opaque strings: a UUID from a database, a ULID from a
log line, a KSUID from an event stream, a Snowflake from a chat platform.
Each one carries information, often a creation time, sometimes a node or a
counter. Reading it means knowing which format the string is, and that is
the step most code guesses at.

zuid is a complete UUID implementation for R, with the formats around it.
The core is [RFC 9562](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9562) in full:
versions 1 to 8, nil and max, and every text form. Around it are the same
128 bits in other alphabets, and fourteen kindred formats: ULID, TypeID,
UPID, SCRU128, SCRU64, KSUID, Snowflake and Sonyflake, XID, ObjectId,
NanoID, Cuid2, Sqids and CID. One `id_` vocabulary works across all of
them.

* **Detection never guesses.** A string that could be two formats is `NA`,
  with the candidates listed. A hint settles it.
* **Inspection never raises on input.** `id_valid()`, `id_fields()` and
  `id_time()` return `NA` for what they cannot read.
* **128 bits do not make a UUID.** A ULID's bytes stay a ULID until you
  convert them, and converting is explicit.
* **Entropy comes from the operating system.** `set.seed()` never changes
  a generated identifier. Tests pass the random bytes in instead.
* **No `Imports`.** The C code is the package's own, checked against the
  reference vectors of each format that publishes them.

## Installation

zuid is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zuid")
```

## Usage

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(zuid)
```

`id_detect()` names the format of each string. The lowercase ULID could
also be a TypeID without a prefix, so its answer is `NA`:

```{r}
ids <- c(
  "018f6b1c-2d3e-7a4b-8c5d-6e7f8091a2b3",
  "01ARZ3NDEKTSV4RRFFQ69G5FAV",
  "01arz3ndektsv4rrffq69g5fav",
  "0ujtsYcgvSTl8PAuAdqWYSMnLOv"
)
found <- id_detect(ids)
as.vector(found)
attr(found, "candidates")[[3]]
```

`id_parse()` gives a typed vector, and `id_time()` reads the creation time
each format records:

```{r}
uuid <- id_parse(ids[1])
uuid
id_time(uuid)
id_time(id_parse(ids[4], "ksuid"))
```

`id_fields()` reads everything else a format knows. A Snowflake means
nothing without its layout, so the layout is an argument:

```{r}
discord <- id_layout("discord")
discord
id_fields(id_parse("175928847299117063", "snowflake", layout = discord))[
  c("time", "node", "sequence")
]
```

The same 16 bytes can be written in other alphabets, read back, or carried
into another format:

```{r}
id_format(uuid, "base58")
id_format(uuid, "words")
id_parse("CB7z5qdx3BKrzyaKnqWbU", "uuid", form = "base58")
id_convert(uuid, "typeid", prefix = "user")
```

Generators read the clock and the operating system's entropy once per call.
Version 7 UUIDs and ULIDs are monotonic within a session:

```{r}
id_uuid(3)
id_ulid(2)
```

Every function starts with `id_` and takes the vector first. A function
that inspects returns `NA` where the input says nothing; a function that
builds raises a classed `zuid_error`.

## Learn more

* [Reading what an identifier knows](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuid/articles/fields.html)
  covers detection, the three validation levels, fields and time.
* [A UUID in every alphabet](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuid/articles/alphabets.html)
  covers the encodings and conversion between formats.
* The [reference index](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuid/reference/) lists
  every function.

## Acknowledgements

zuid is checked against the reference vectors of RFC 9562, TypeID's
`valid.yml` and `invalid.yml`, Discord's Snowflake example, and the
specifications or reference implementations of ULID, UPID, SCRU128, SCRU64,
KSUID, XID, Sqids, NanoID, Proquint, Niceware and multiformats CID. The Sqids blocklist and the Niceware word list are data
from their upstream projects; `inst/COPYRIGHTS` names their sources and
authors.
